Class SerialServerSocket

java.lang.Object
com.sgware.serialsoc.SerialServerSocket
All Implemented Interfaces:
CheckedRunnable, AutoCloseable, Callable<Void>
Direct Known Subclasses:
SimpleSerialServerSocket
public abstract class SerialServerSocket extends Object implements CheckedRunnable, AutoCloseable
A serial server socket listens for incoming socket connections and ensures all inputs from them are processed one at a time on a single thread. It also guarantees that certain methods run in order, including setup and shutdown methods for the server and each socket, even if an exception is thrown.

When run() is called, all of the following events will happen:

  • onStart() is called first on the same thread that called run(). If it throws an exception, no other methods will run.
  • connect() is called on the same thread that called run() to establish a server socket. If it does not throw an exception, onConnect() is called on the same thread that called run().
  • If connect() did not throw an exception, the server starts a new thread that continuously calls accept() to wait for new connections. Each time a new socket is accepted, the server calls create(Socket) on the same thread that called run() to wrap a SerialSocket around the new socket. If create(Socket) throws an exception, the socket is closed and never reported to the server. If create(Socket) does not throw an exception, the new socket is reported to the server's onAccept(SerialSocket) method, which runs on the same thread that called run().
  • Each time a new SerialSocket is successfully created, its SerialSocket.onConnect() method is called first on the same thread that called run().
  • If SerialSocket.onConnect() did not throw an exception, a new thread continuously calls SerialSocket.read() to listen for new input. Each input that is successfully received is reported to SerialSocket.receive(String), which runs on the same thread that called run().
  • If the server needs to run an operation regularly, you can Thread.start() a Clock that will regularly call tick() on the server and SerialSocket.tick() on each of its sockets from the same thread that called run().
  • A socket can be closed by the client, by a network problem, because one of its methods threw an exception, or by calling SerialSocket.close() from any thread. Regardless of how it is closed, SerialSocket.onClose(), then SerialSocket.disconnect(), then SerialSocket.onDisconnect() are always called in that order from the same thread that called run(). These methods always run even if an earlier method threw an exception.
  • If any SerialSocket methods throw an exception, the exception is reported to SerialSocket.onException(Exception) on the same thread that called run(), and then the socket will close gracefully. SerialSocket.onException(Exception) can either ignore the exception or re-throw it to cause the server to shut down.
  • If any SerialServerSocket methods throw an exception (or if SerialSocket.onException(Exception) re-throws an exception), the exception is reported to onException(Exception) on the same thread that called run(), and then the server will shut down gracefully.
  • A server shuts down when one of its methods throws an exception, when a network problem causes the server to disconnect, when the JVM shuts down, or when close() is called from any thread. Regardless of how it is closed, if connect() did not throw an exception, onClose(), then disconnect(), then onDisconnect() are always called in that order from the same thread that called run().
  • As long as onStart() did not throw an exception, onStop() is always called last from the same thread that called run().
  • If an exception was thrown by any of the server's methods, it is thrown by run() after all of the shut down methods have completed.
You can check the server's Status with getStatus(). You can also check if a server has ever had a status with has(Status) or wait for a status with await(Status). For example, you can check if the server has Status.CONNECTED or wait for it to connect.

If another thread needs to execute something on the thread that called run() that cannot be written into one of the above methods, it can call execute(CheckedRunnable) to run a CheckedRunnable on the main thread.

Stephen G. Ware

  • Method Details

    • getStatus

      public Status getStatus()
      Returns the server's current Status. If run() has not yet been called, this method returns null. Otherwise, it returns:
      • Status.RUN if run() has been called but onStart() has not yet completed.
      • Status.STARTED if onStart() completed successfully but the server has not yet connected.
      • Status.CONNECTED if connect() completed successfully and the server has not yet been closed.
      • Status.CLOSED if close() has been called, or if the server has closed automatically for another reason (like an exception or a network problem) but has not yet disconnected.
      • Status.DISCONNECTED if the server previously connected and disconnect() has completed (successfully or not).
      • Status.FINISHED if the server previously disconnected, is shutting down, and is no longer accepting operations via execute(CheckedRunnable).
      • Status.STOPPED if onStart() threw an exception or after onStop() has completed (successfully or not) and no more events will happen for this server.
      Returns:
      the server's current status

    • has

      public boolean has(Status status)
      Checks whether the server has ever achieved the given status. For example, this method can be used to check whether the server ever Status.CONNECTED.
      Parameters:
      status - the status in question
      Returns:
      true if the server has ever had that status, false otherwise

    • await

      public boolean await(Status status) throws InterruptedException
      Waits for the server to have the given status, or for it to become impossible for the server to have that status. For example, you can await the Status.CONNECTED status. Once the server connects successfully, the method will return true. If the server fails to connect, this method will wait until the server fails to connect and return false.
      Parameters:
      status - the status in question
      Returns:
      true when the status occurs, or false when it becomes impossible to achieve the status
      Throws:
      InterruptedException - if the thread that called this method is interrupted while waiting for the status

    • onStart

      protected void onStart() throws Exception
      Always runs first when the server starts. It runs on the same thread that called run(). Unless this method throws an exception, onStop() is guaranteed to run before the server stops.

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs

    • connect

      protected abstract void connect() throws Exception
      Binds the server socket to its network port. It runs after onStart() on the same thread that called run(). If this method does not throw an exception, onConnect(), onClose(), disconnect(), and onDisconnect() are guaranteed to run before the server stops.
      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs when the server connects to the network

    • onConnect

      protected void onConnect() throws Exception
      Runs after connect() (if it did not throw an exception) on the same thread that called run().

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs

    • accept

      protected abstract Socket accept() throws Exception
      Blocks until a new socket connects to the server and then returns it. This method does not run on the same thread that called run(). Once this method returns a socket, it does not run again until after create(Socket) and onAccept(SerialSocket) have finished processing the socket. If this method throws an exception, the server closes.
      Returns:
      a newly accepted socket
      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs while waiting for or accepting the new socket connection

    • create

      protected abstract SerialSocket create(Socket socket) throws Exception
      Creates a SerialSocket from a Socket. This method is called after accept() but on the same thread that called run(). If this method throws an exception, the socket will be closed; otherwise, onAccept(SerialSocket) will be called after.
      Parameters:
      socket - the socket to make into a serial socket
      Returns:
      a serial socket
      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs while creating the serial socket

    • onAccept

      protected void onAccept(SerialSocket socket) throws Exception
      Runs each time a new SerialSocket connects to the server on the same thread that called run().

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      Parameters:
      socket - the newly created serial socket
      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs

    • tick

      protected void tick() throws Exception
      If a Clock is started for this server, this method is called regularly on each interval by the same thread that called run().

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs

    • onException

      protected void onException(Exception exception) throws Exception
      If an exception is thrown at any time by one of the server's methods, it is reported to this method from the same thread that called run() (regardless of which thread the exception was thrown on).

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      While this method declares an exception for convenience, if it throws an exception that exception is ignored; otherwise, the server could get trapped in an infinite loop of this method throwing exceptions and then reporting them back to this method.

      Parameters:
      exception - the exception that was thrown by one of the server methods
      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs while processing the exception

    • close

      public final void close()
      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable

    • onClose

      protected void onClose() throws Exception
      Runs after the server is closed, either because a method threw an exception, because a network problem disconnected the server, because the JVM shut down, or because close() was called. This method only runs if the server successfully connected and it runs on the same thread that called run().

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs

    • disconnect

      protected abstract void disconnect() throws Exception
      Disconnects the server from the network such that it can no longer accept any new connections. This method should cause accept() to stop blocking if it is waiting. This method runs after onClose() on the same thread that called run(), but only if the server successfully connected. It is possible the server is already disconnected from the network by the time this method runs if a network error is what caused the server to close.
      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs while disconnecting the server from the network

    • onDisconnect

      protected void onDisconnect() throws Exception
      Runs after disconnect() on the same thread that called run(). This method only runs if the server successfully connected, and it runs regardless of whether disconnect() threw an exception. No new sockets will connect to the server after this method runs, but some sockets may still be connected when it runs.

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs

    • onStop

      protected void onStop() throws Exception
      Always runs last just before the server stops. It runs on the same thread that called run() but only if the server started.

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs
